content.text: /ext:medcp In HBeAg-positive chronic HBV, nucleotide vs nucleoside polymerase inhibitors regimens show different 180-day HBV-DNA undetectable rates?
I'll investigate this by exploring the clinical database structure first, then querying for HBeAg-positive chronic HBV patients on these two drug classes.

This is an OMOP CDM database. Let me find the relevant drug concepts (nucleotide analogs: tenofovir/adefovir; nucleoside analogs: entecavir/lamivudine/telbivudine), the HBeAg-positive marker, and the HBV-DNA measurement concepts.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT concept_id, concept_name, domain_id, vocabulary_id, concept_class_id, standard_concept
FROM omop.concept
WHERE lower(concept_name) LIKE '%tenofovir%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%adefovir%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%entecavir%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%telbivudine%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%lamivudine%'
ORDER BY vocabulary_id, concept_name
LIMIT 200;

SELECT concept_id, concept_name, domain_id, vocabulary_id, concept_class_id, standard_concept
FROM omop.concept
WHERE lower(concept_name) LIKE '%hepatitis b%dna%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%hbv%dna%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%hepatitis b virus dna%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%hbeag%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%hepatitis b e antigen%'
ORDER BY domain_id, concept_name
LIMIT 200;

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT TOP 200 concept_id, concept_name, domain_id, vocabulary_id, concept_class_id, standard_concept
FROM omop.concept
WHERE lower(concept_name) LIKE '%tenofovir%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%adefovir%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%entecavir%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%telbivudine%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%lamivudine%'
ORDER BY vocabulary_id, concept_name;

SELECT TOP 200 concept_id, concept_name, domain_id, vocabulary_id, concept_class_id, standard_concept
FROM omop.concept
WHERE lower(concept_name) LIKE '%hepatitis b%dna%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%hbv%dna%'
   OR lower(concept_name) LIKE '%hbeag%'

arguments.sql_query:
-- First treatment start per person for each drug class (nucleotide vs nucleoside),
-- restricted to persons who ever had HBeAg antigen testing (proxy for HBeAg-assessed CHB).
-- Outcome: any HBV-DNA quantitative test in the 150-210 day window after first drug start,
-- with the minimum value in that window <= detection floor (undetectable ~ <1.9 log IU/mL i.e. <~80 IU/mL).
WITH hbeag_tested AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT person_id
  FROM omop.measurement
  WHERE measurement_concept_id IN (2213089, 4209123, 40302980, 40324731, 37397806)
),
class_start AS (
  SELECT de.person_id,
         CASE WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (21603166,1123612,21603167) THEN 'nucleotide'
              WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (21603169,21603164,21603170) THEN 'nucleoside' END AS drug_class,
         MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS first_start
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (21603166,1123612,21603167,21603169,21603164,21603170)
    AND de.person_id IN (SELECT person_id FROM hbeag_tested)
  GROUP BY de.person_id,
         CASE WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (21603166,1123612,21603167) THEN 'nucleotide'
              WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (21603169,21603164,21603170) THEN 'nucleoside' END
),
dna AS (
  SELECT person_id, measurement_date, value_as_number
  FROM omop.measurement
  WHERE measurement_concept_id IN (3027346,3049385,3052981,3026949,3046542,3043634,3048505,3008652,3017028,3045140,3014700,3032567)
    AND value_as_number IS NOT NULL
),
followup AS (
  SELECT cs.person_id, cs.drug_class, cs.first_start,
         MIN(d.value_as_number) AS min_dna_180
  FROM class_start cs
  LEFT JOIN dna d
    ON d.person_id = cs.person_id
   AND d.measurement_date BETWEEN DATEADD(day,150,cs.first_start) AND DATEADD(day,210,cs.first_start)
  GROUP BY cs.person_id, cs.drug_class, cs.first_start
)
SELECT drug_class,
       COUNT(*) AS n_started,
       SUM(CASE WHEN min_dna_180 IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_180d_dna,
       SUM(CASE WHEN min_dna_180 <= 1.9 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_undetectable
FROM followup
GROUP BY drug_class;

The cohort is very small, but here are the results.

## HBeAg-assessed chronic HBV: 180-day HBV-DNA undetectable rates

Among patients who had HBeAg antigen testing (proxy for HBeAg-assessed CHB) and started a first-line oral polymerase inhibitor, with an HBV-DNA quantitative result in the 150–210 day window (undetectable ≈ <1.9 log IU/mL):

| Regimen class | Started | With 180-day HBV-DNA | Undetectable | Rate (of tested) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Nucleoside** (entecavir, lamivudine, telbivudine) | 148 | 33 | 6 | **18.2%** (6/33) |
| **Nucleotide** (TDF, TAF, adefovir) | 111 | 19 | 3 | **15.8%** (3/19) |

**Bottom line:** In this database the 180-day undetectable rates are numerically similar (18% nucleoside vs 16% nucleotide) — no meaningful difference. With only 33 vs 19 evaluable patients, this is far too small to detect a real difference (Fisher's exact p ≈ 1.0), so the data cannot confirm or refute a class effect.

**Important caveats about what could be measured:**
- **HBeAg positivity could not be isolated.** The HBeAg qualitative result is not stored in any structured value field (`value_as_concept_id`, `value_as_number`, `value_source_value` are all null). I used "had HBeAg testing" as a proxy for HBeAg-assessed CHB — it does **not** confirm HBeAg-*positive* status, so the true HBeAg-positive subgroup cannot be defined here.
- **Attrition is severe:** only ~22% (nucleoside) and ~17% (nucleotide) of starters had an HBV-DNA test in the exact 150–210 day window, so the denominators are the tested minority, not intent-to-treat.
- Regimen classes are assigned on first exposure; combination/switch therapy and adherence aren't accounted for.

If you want, I can widen the window (e.g., 90–270 days), use "last value carried forward," or express undetectable as intent-to-treat (undetectable / all starters) — but the HBeAg-positive restriction itself isn't recoverable from structured data in this instance.
